title: Evaluating and Enhancing Large Language Models for Novelty Assessment in Scholarly Publications

bias_targets.methodology: Swapping the presentation order of the two compared research papers in the prompt to measure if the LLM disproportionately favors the first or second paper regardless of actual content.

Appending different university affiliations (a top research university vs. a teaching university) to the compared papers and swapping these affiliations to observe if the model preferentially assesses papers from the top university as more novel.

Comparing the LLM's novelty assessment accuracy across six different scholarly fields (e.g., Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics) to identify performance disparities linked to training data domain imbalances.
